newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent slides, Forties firms in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent slides, Forties firms in brisk trade.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mostly weaker on Thursday as benchmark Dated Brent shed 15 cents under the weight of unsold late February barrels, traders said.
But Forties added a couple of cents to its premium as U.S. and European refiners snapped up at least three million barrels in a continuation of Wednesday's buying spree.
A Feb 25-27 Brent was sold to a European major for March Brent -10 cents after a Feb 26-28 loader fetched +5 cents on Wednesday.
Traders said the discount could widen even further with at least two other end month cargoes still available.
The first cargoes from the March programme -- which was set at 42 full cargoes and 1.93 million barrels in top-ups -- are due to be nominated loading dates on Friday.
The only other North Sea programme released on Thursday was for Norwegian Gullfaks, showing 24 cargoes were due to load in March, up two from February.

A U.S. major bought Forties loading Mar 3-5, Mar 6-8 and Mar 11-13 for between Dated Brent +40 and +44 cents, while European refiners bought cargoes loading Feb 27-Mar 1 and Mar 4-6 for +42 and +40 cents respectively.

Intermonth paper spreads were steady after dipping in early trade, Mar/Apr moving back up to +33 cents from +28 cents in brisk dealing. Nearby CFDs shed nine cents, reflecting weaker Brent market sentiment.
West African markets were muted with buyers reluctant to show bids and meagre amounts on offer. Bonny Light was steady at about Dated Brent +60/70 but Qua Iboe was some five cents lower.
A Forcados loading March 1-10 was done at Dated Brent +60, down five cents from last week but a strong number for the distillate-rich grade in view of recent pressure on gas oil, traders said.
